originalTitle: CoreWeave shares tumble as bond yields near 15% on concern about AI borrowing binge
summary: Shares of CoreWeave sank 15%, while yields in its bonds blew out further.
content:
CoreWeave's stock and bonds were both hit on Wednesday as investor fear grew that some technology companies are borrowing too heavily for the artificial intelligence build-out.

Shares of the so-called neocloud nosedived 15.5%, while yields on its debt jumped higher. The yield to maturity on its 9.625% bond due in 2032 is sitting at 14.8%, while that of its 9.75% bond due in 2031 is around 14.9%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

CEO Mike Intrator dismissed the market moves in a memo obtained by CNBC.

"When you are building a new type of technology company there will be periods of time when the market misunderstands and acts irrationally," he wrote. "We are confident in our backlog which more than supports all of our debt obligations."

While investors were once excited about getting in on the AI action, investor sentiment has started to shift, said Luis Alvarado, co-head of global fixed income strategy at Wells Fargo Investment Institute.

Now, investors are demanding more risk compensation, he said.

"The era of easy money, which we experienced in the first nine months of the year, is starting to disappear and dissipate," Alvarado noted. "Now the extra dollar or the marginal dollar is going to be more looked at with a microscope into the concessions that the issuer is giving you back."

Tech investor Chamath Palihapitiya , founder and CEO of investment firm Social Capital and CEO of AI company 8090, called out CoreWeave's soaring yields on X late Tuesday. That prompted Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to respond, "yikes."

Palihapitiya shared a chart of the 2032 bond, noting that the yield "touched 15%" and then "closed at a new high" on Tuesday. He also included part of his deep dive into whether the AI build-out is creating a private credit bubble, in which he noted "how little extra lenders appear to charge for AI risk."

CoreWeave's balance sheet is "relatively bad" compared to its neocloud peers, said Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets. That's because CoreWeave has done more borrowing and is currently building more data centers, he explained.

"The yields have blown out because there's just more and more concern — that I don't share — about the wherewithal of these guys [being] able to over time pay back their interest expense," Meeks said.

"It's definitely not a deteriorating situation," he added. "Maybe it's not improving, and I didn't really expect it to improve until these data centers get up and running."

He expects the company to report flat margins from June to September and guide for margins to have a pretty significant improvement between September and December. CoreWeave's next quarterly results are expected in November.

CoreWeave's overall credit rating is a B+ at S&P Credit Ratings, which is junk bond territory. With rates in general having risen lately, it's natural that highly-leveraged companies, such as CoreWeave, are affected, said Gavan Nolan, executive director of fixed income pricing at S&P Global Market Intelligence.

CoreWeave "has capital expenditure levels that are almost hyperscaler-like, but it doesn't have the hyperscaler balance sheet," Nolan said.

CoreWeave isn't the only tech company seeing fallout from concerns over AI debt loads. For instance, shares of Oracle closed down nearly 9% on Wednesday. Yields on its bonds were also higher, with the yield to maturity on its 6.25% bond due in Nov. 2032 sitting at 7.24%.

The overall tech sector brought down the stock market on Wednesday with the Nasdaq Composite closing down 1.9%. The debt concern seems to be hitting the shakier stocks outside of the "Magnificent Seven" the hardest.

Another neocloud stock, Nebius , dropped 10%. Dell cratered by roughly 11%.

Companies are in a race to build AI infrastructure and have turned to the credit market to finance their projects, leading to surging supply of new bonds.

For instance, hyperscalers Alphabet , Amazon , Meta Platforms and Oracle together have issued more than $228 billion in bonds, as of Oct. 13, according to LSEG. That is more than double the amount seen in all of 2025. All but Oracle have investment-grade ratings at S&P Credit Ratings.

Overall, hyperscalers are on track to spend $800 billion this year, according to JPMorgan . By 2027, it is expected to exceed $1 trillion annually, the bank said.

— CNBC's Seema Mody contributed reporting.
chineseTitle: 由于担心 AI 借贷热潮，债券收益率接近 15%，CoreWeave 股价暴跌
chineseSummary: CoreWeave 股价下跌 15%，而其债券收​​益率进一步飙升。
chineseContent:
由于投资者越来越担心一些科技公司为人工智能建设而举债过多，CoreWeave 的股票和债券周三均受到打击。

Neocloud 的股价暴跌 15.5%，而其债务收益率则大幅上涨。 2032年到期的9.625%债券的到期收益率为14.8%，2031年到期的9.75%债券的到期收益率约为14.9%。债券收益率与价格成反比。

首席执行官 Mike Intrator 在 CNBC 获得的一份备忘录中驳斥了市场走势。

他写道：“当你建立一家新型科技公司时，市场有时会产生误解并出现非理性行为。” “我们对我们的积压订单充满信心，这足以支持我们所有的债务义务。”

富国银行投资研究所全球固定收益策略联席主管路易斯·阿尔瓦拉多 (Luis Alvarado) 表示，虽然投资者一度对参与人工智能行动感到兴奋，但投资者情绪已开始发生转变。

他说，现在，投资者要求更多的风险补偿。

阿尔瓦拉多指出：“我们在今年前九个月经历的轻松赚钱的时代正在开始消失。” “现在，额外的美元或边际美元将被更多地用显微镜来审视发行人给予你的让步。”

科技投资者、投资公司 Social Capital 创始人兼首席执行官、人工智能公司 8090 首席执行官 Chamath Palihapitiya 周二晚间对 CoreWeave 收益率飙升表示赞赏。这促使特斯拉和 SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克回应“哎呀”。

Palihapitiya 分享了 2032 年债券的图表，指出收益率“触及 15%”，然后在周二“收于新高”。他还深入探讨了人工智能的发展是否正在造成私人信贷泡沫，其中他指出“贷款机构似乎很少对人工智能风险收取额外费用”。

Freedom Capital Markets 技术研究主管 Paul Meeks 表示，与 Neocloud 同行相比，CoreWeave 的资产负债表“相对较差”。他解释说，这是因为 CoreWeave 已经进行了更多的借贷，目前正在建设更多的数据中心。

米克斯说：“收益率飙升是因为人们越来越担心这些人是否有能力随着时间的推移偿还利息费用，但我不这么认为。”

“情况绝对不会恶化，”他补充道。 “也许情况并没有改善，而且在这些数据中心启动并运行之前，我并没有真正期望它会改善。”

他预计该公司 6 月至 9 月的利润率将持平，并预计 9 月至 12 月的利润率将有相当大的改善。 CoreWeave 的下一季度业绩预计将于 11 月公布。

CoreWeave 的整体信用评级为标准普尔信用评级 B+，属于垃圾债券领域。标准普尔全球市场情报公司固定收益定价执行董事加万·诺兰表示，随着最近利率普遍上升，像CoreWeave这样的高杠杆公司自然会受到影响。

诺兰表示，CoreWeave“的资本支出水平几乎与超大规模企业类似，但它没有超大规模企业的资产负债表”。

CoreWeave 并不是唯一一家因人工智能债务负担而受到影响的科技公司。例如，甲骨文股价周三收盘下跌近 9%。其债券收益率也较高，2032 年 11 月到期、利率为 6.25% 的债券到期收益率为 7.24%。

周三，整个科技板块拖累股市下跌，纳斯达克综合指数收盘下跌 1.9%。债务担忧似乎对“七巨头”之外的那些摇摇欲坠的股票造成了最严重的打击。

另一只 neocloud 股票 Nebius 下跌 10%。戴尔股价下跌约 11%。

各公司竞相建设人工智能基础设施，并转向信贷市场为其项目融资，导致新债券供应激增。

例如，根据 LSEG 的数据，截至 10 月 13 日，超大型企业 Alphabet、亚马逊、Meta Platforms 和 Oracle 总共发行了超过 2280 亿美元的债券。这是 2025 年全年金额的两倍多。除甲骨文外，所有公司均获得标准普尔信用评级的投资级评级。

摩根大通表示，总体而言，超大规模企业今年有望支出 8000 亿美元。该银行表示，到 2027 年，预计每年将超过 1 万亿美元。

— CNBC 的 Seema Mody 贡献了报道。
